Wed Oct 28, 2026 9:00 am—12:30 pm

Telling Stories with Maps: Bringing Map-Making into the Classroom

This series of two workshops is designed for instructors who want to help students use maps and map-based storytelling in their coursework. Over the course of two sessions, we will demystify the process of creating interactive maps and equip participants with the tools and resources they need to teach basic map-making in the classroom.

Participants will create an interactive map-story based on a topic of their own choosing and work through the process from start to finish. By the end of the two-part workshop, they will have a working map-story of their own creation, as well as a better understanding of how to guide students through a similar project over the course of a semester.

The workshop will be led by Aaron Reiss(Link is external), a journalist and cartographer, former Yale instructor, and current Yale Library Geospatial Expert-on-Call(Link is external). Aaron will introduce a practical workflow for creating interactive map-based stories using open-source tools, as well as Esri StoryMaps, which you know well! His approach goes beyond making maps, helping students use maps, data, and narratives to develop arguments and tell compelling stories, with minimal coding.

The workshop includes:

  • Part I: How Maps Work (Virtual): October 20, 12:00 - 1:30 PM (recording will be available).
  • Part II:  Hands-On Map Making (In person): October 28, 9:00 AM-12:30 PM (Part I attendance or viewing the recording is required) LOCATION: DH Lab, Sterling Memorial Library

Co-hosted by the Yale Library and the Yale Center for Geospatial Solutions
